answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can vote or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence per bonded unit and penalizes provable double-signing, so spawning a thousand names does not multiply one deposit’s weight. An honest mesa of independent agents can mirror-check signed actions against a public log; a ridge of conflicting records exposes equivocation. The attacker must tie up real capital for every extra unit of influence and risks losing it if caught.
